힘들었어요.en: It was hard, I had a hard time.

texto.@es: **-고 해서** introduce una razón o circunstancia entre otras posibles: 좋다 → **좋고 해서** (como además hacía buen tiempo), 피곤하다 → **피곤하고 해서** (como además estaba cansado). Es frecuente en conversación, pero no es simplemente una versión informal de «porque».
texto.@en: **-고 해서** introduce una razón o circunstancia entre otras posibles: 좋다 → **좋고 해서** (como además hacía buen tiempo), 피곤하다 → **피곤하고 해서** (como además estaba cansado). It is common in conversation, but it is not simply an informal version of «because».

texto: 날씨도 **좋고 해서** 공원에 갔어요 = como además hacía buen tiempo, fuimos al parque.

texto.@es: **-아/어서** suele unir directamente una causa y su consecuencia. **-고 해서** presenta una razón de manera más abierta, a menudo con otras circunstancias implícitas.
texto.@en: **-아/어서** often directly links a cause and its consequence. **-고 해서** presents a reason more openly, often with other implicit circumstances.

texto.@es: 약속도 있고 해서 먼저 갈게요 = como también tengo otro compromiso, me iré primero.
texto.@en: 약속도 있고 해서 먼저 갈게요 = as I also have another commitment, I will leave first.

frases.ko: 오늘은 날씨가 좋고 해서 공원에 갔어요.
frases.es: Hoy hacía buen tiempo, así que fuimos al parque.
frases.en: It was a good time today, so we went to the park.

analisis.@en: as it was a good weather

frases.en: Ugh, it must have been good!

frases.es: Sí, pero hacía tanto calor que fue duro.
frases.en: Yeah, but it was so hot it was hard.

frases.es: Por eso, la próxima vez vayamos por la tarde.
frases.en: That's why next time we go in the afternoon.

pregunta.@en: What does «날씨가 좋고 해서 공원에 갔어요» mean?

texto.@es: Como hacía buen tiempo, fuimos al parque.
texto.@en: As it was a good time ago, we went to the park.

explicacion.@es: 좋고 해서 = como hacía buen tiempo.
explicacion.@en: 좋고 해서 = as it was good weather.

texto.@es: Hacía buen tiempo y no fuimos al parque.
texto.@en: It was a good time, and we didn't go to the park.

explicacion.@en: That would be 좋았는데 안 갔어요.

texto.@es: Iremos al parque si hace buen tiempo.
texto.@en: We'll go to the park if it's a good time.

explicacion.@es: Eso sería 날씨가 좋으면 갈 거예요.
explicacion.@en: That would be 날씨가 좋으면 갈 거예요.
바쁘고 해서 = how busy I was.
It's «if you're busy».
It's «Because I was busy.», more neutral.

texto.@es: Como estaba cansado, me acosté temprano.
texto.@en: Since I was tired, I slept early.

explicacion.@en: 피곤하고 해서 = because I was tired.

texto.@es: Me acosté temprano y luego estoy cansado.
texto.@en: I went to bed early and then I'm tired.

explicacion.@en: The order is the other way around.

texto.@es: Estoy cansado, así que no duermo.
texto.@en: I'm tired, so I don't sleep.

explicacion.@en: That would be 피곤해서 안 자요.

pregunta.@en: Why did they go to the park?

texto.@en: Because it was a good time.

explicacion.@es: 좋고 해서 = como hacía buen tiempo.
explicacion.@en: 좋고 해서 = as it was good weather.
That would be 비가 와서.
That would be 시간이 없어서.

explicacion.@es: 가고 해서 = porque fui. 먹었어요 = comí.
explicacion.@en: 가고 해서 = because I went. 먹었어요 = I ate.

pregunta.@es: ¿Cómo dices «porque estoy ocupado» (바쁘다) en tono familiar?
pregunta.@en: How do you say «Because I'm busy.» (바쁘다) in a family tone?

explicacion.@en: It's «Because I'm busy.», more neutral.
It's «I'm busy.».
더워서 = because it was hot.
It's «if it's hot».
It's «It was hot.», no cause.

explicacion.@es: 힘들었어요 = fue duro, lo pasé mal.
explicacion.@en: 힘들었어요 = was hard, I had a hard time.
That would be 재미있었어요.
That would be 쉬웠어요.
